newsitem.title: IRAN: Tajik government, opposition sign accords - Iran.
newsitem.headline: Tajik government, opposition sign accords - Iran.

text.p: Tajikistan's President Imomali Rakhmonov and opposition leader Sayid Abdullo Nuri signed accords on Friday after talks in Iran on achieving peace in the turbulent Central Asian country, state-run Tehran radio said.

It said the two leaders signed the accords, including an agreement on each side's quota in a future Commission of National Reconciliation, at the end of their two-day talks in the northeastern city of Mashhad.

The composition of the commission and the issue of disarming opposition forces have been among outstanding differences after accords reached by the Moscow-backed government and the Islamist opposition in two earlier rounds of talks since December.

Speaking about the Mashhad accords, Iranian Foreign Minister Ali Akbar Velayati said: "The opposition forces would not be disarmed as long as a lasting stability has not been established", Iran's news agency IRNA reported.
The two sides also issued a statement condemning "all terroristic acts" in Tajikistan, IRNA said.

This was in reference to a spate of assassinations last week and a two-week crisis in which Tajik rebels seized hostages to pressure the government to allow a group of their men to join them from neighbouring Afghanistan.

On Tuesday, gunmen killed seven people in the Tajik capital Dushanbe, a day after the rebels released their hostages. Five of those shot were ethnic Russians. Moscow has thousands of peacekeeping troops in the volatile country.

A ceasefire, also part of the earlier accords, appears to be holding after a four-year civil war that killed tens of thousands of people and displaced thousands of others in the former Soviet republic of nearly six million.
